# System for Monitoring the Closing Unit Position of an Injection-Molding Machine

## Overview

The present invention provides a system designed to monitor the position of the closing unit of an injection-molding machine. A distinctive feature of this system is that it achieves reliable position monitoring by bypassing the light curtain that is conventionally employed to secure the closing unit and the surrounding tool area. By replacing or supplementing this safety mechanism, the system enables continued operation and precise supervision of the closing unit during specific process steps where the standard light-curtain protection would otherwise interfere.

## Molding Tool Configuration

The injection-molding machine operates with at least one molding tool. This tool is composed of two or more parts that, when brought together, enclose at least one mold cavity. The cavity defines the geometry of the molded component and is filled with material during the injection process. The proper alignment and spacing of these tool parts relative to one another is critical to ensuring both product quality and safe machine operation.

## Control and Monitoring Architecture

At the heart of the system is a programmable logic controller (PLC), which operates in conjunction with a dedicated movement monitoring module, referred to as the MOC. Together, these components provide indirect monitoring of the position of the closing unit and, by extension, the relative positioning of the individual tool parts. Rather than relying on direct observation of the tool interface, the system infers positional data through the coordinated action of the PLC and the MOC, allowing for continuous and automated supervision throughout the molding cycle.

## Sensor Integration

To gather the necessary positional information, the system employs distance measuring sticks that function as sensors. These sensors generate signals corresponding to the measured distances within the closing unit. The signals are transmitted to and processed by the PLC via the MOC, ensuring that accurate, real-time positional data is available to the control system at all times.

## The Bumping Step and Safety Threshold

A key phase of the process addressed by this system is the so-called bumping step. This step occurs after the closing pressure has been fully built up and the mold cavity has been filled with material. During bumping, the tool parts are required to maintain a spacing gap that remains below a specified maximum value. The system continuously monitors this gap through the sensor arrangement described above. Should the spacing exceed the predetermined maximum threshold, the system responds by automatically shutting off the machine. This safeguard prevents improper tool separation and ensures that the molding process proceeds only within safe and controlled operating parameters.

# Position Monitoring System for Injection-Molding Machine Closing Units

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a system for monitoring the position of the closing unit and the molding tool parts of an injection-molding machine. More specifically, the invention pertains to a monitoring arrangement that employs distance measuring sticks as sensors, the signals of which are processed by a programmable logic controller (PLC) through a dedicated movement monitoring module, notably while bypassing the conventional safety light curtain.

## Background of the Invention

Injection-molding machines conventionally rely on safety light curtains to protect operators and equipment during the operation of the closing unit. However, during certain phases of the molding cycle—particularly the so-called "bumping" step that follows the filling of the mold—precise control over the relative position of the molding tool parts becomes critical. In this phase, the tool parts must maintain a defined and limited separation to ensure both product quality and safe operation. Conventional safety mechanisms are not always suited to provide the fine-grained positional monitoring required during this specific stage of the process.

## Summary of the Invention

To address these limitations, the invention provides a system in which distance measuring sticks function as position sensors mounted in relation to the closing unit and the molding tool parts. The signals generated by these sensors are transmitted to a programmable logic controller, where they are processed by a movement monitoring module. Significantly, this processing occurs while bypassing the safety light curtain, allowing the system to perform dedicated positional monitoring independent of the standard safety curtain function during the relevant phase of operation.

The central purpose of the system is to ensure that the molding tool parts maintain a specified maximal spacing gap during the bumping step, which takes place after the mold has been filled. The movement monitoring module continuously compares the measured distance against this predefined maximal value. Should the actual spacing exceed the specified threshold, the system responds by automatically shutting off the machine.

## Advantages of the Invention

By continuously monitoring the relative position of the tool parts and enforcing a maximal permissible gap during the critical bumping phase, the system significantly enhances both operational safety and precision. The automatic shutoff function prevents the tool parts from separating beyond the acceptable limit, thereby reducing the risk of defective products and potential hazards. Integrating the distance measuring sticks with a programmable logic controller and a dedicated movement monitoring module—while bypassing the safety light curtain—allows for reliable, precise, and phase-specific position control that conventional safety arrangements alone cannot provide.

# The Role of PLC Systems in Management of Change (MOC)

## Introduction

In modern industrial environments, the **Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)** stands as one of the most critical components of automation infrastructure. When changes are made to these systems, the **Management of Change (MOC)** process becomes essential to ensure safety, reliability, and compliance. Understanding how these two elements interact is fundamental for engineers, plant managers, and safety professionals.

## What Is a PLC?

The Programmable Logic Controller is a ruggedized industrial computer designed to control manufacturing processes, machinery, and other automated systems. PLCs continuously monitor input devices—such as sensors and switches—and make decisions based on programmed logic to control output devices like motors, valves, and alarms. Their reliability in harsh environments makes them indispensable across industries including oil and gas, chemical processing, water treatment, and manufacturing.

## Understanding Management of Change (MOC)

The Management of Change is a systematic approach used to review, evaluate, and approve modifications before they are implemented. Whether the change involves equipment, procedures, software, or personnel, the MOC process ensures that potential risks are identified and mitigated. This is particularly important in facilities where uncontrolled changes could lead to safety incidents, environmental damage, or operational failures.

## The Connection Between PLC and MOC

Any modification to a PLC—whether it involves updating the control logic, changing setpoints, or replacing hardware components—must pass through the MOC process. This connection is vital because:

- **Safety implications:** A single error in PLC programming can compromise critical safety functions, potentially endangering workers and equipment.
- **Documentation integrity:** The MOC ensures that all changes are properly recorded, maintaining an accurate history of system modifications.
- **Risk assessment:** Before any PLC change is deployed, the potential consequences are thoroughly evaluated.
- **Regulatory compliance:** Many industries are governed by strict regulations that require formal change management procedures.

## Best Practices

To effectively integrate PLC changes within the MOC framework, organizations should:

1. **Require formal approval** for all programming and configuration changes.
2. **Test modifications** in a controlled environment before deployment.
3. **Maintain version control** to track every revision of PLC programs.
4. **Train personnel** on both the technical and procedural aspects of change management.
5. **Conduct post-implementation reviews** to verify that changes performed as intended.

## Conclusion

The relationship between the PLC and the MOC process highlights the importance of disciplined change management in automated environments. By ensuring that every modification to a PLC follows a structured MOC procedure, organizations can protect their operations, maintain compliance, and—most importantly—safeguard the people and assets under their care.

# Patent Abstract

## Injection-Molding Machine System with PLC-Based Closing Unit Position Monitoring

An injection-molding machine system is disclosed for monitoring the position and movement of a closing unit (mold clamping unit) without reliance on a conventional safety light curtain as the primary position-sensing element. The system comprises one or more distance measuring sticks (linear distance sensors) mounted in operative association with the movable platen of the closing unit, each configured to generate a continuous distance signal representative of the instantaneous position of the closing unit along its travel path. A programmable logic controller (PLC) includes a movement monitoring module that receives and processes the distance signals to determine position, direction of travel, and velocity of the closing unit in real time.

The movement monitoring module compares the sensed positional data against stored threshold values and predefined motion profiles to detect deviations, unexpected movement, or unsafe operating conditions. Upon detection of a fault or out-of-range condition, the PLC generates a control signal to interrupt, decelerate, or halt movement of the closing unit. By employing the distance measuring sticks in cooperation with the PLC-based movement monitoring module, the system enables safe operation of the closing unit while permitting the safety light curtain to be bypassed under defined operating states, thereby maintaining protective monitoring functionality through redundant, sensor-based position verification.

The disclosed system improves operational flexibility and cycle efficiency while preserving a safe working envelope, and is suitable for retrofit or original integration into hydraulic, electric, or hybrid injection-molding machines.

---

**Note:** Bypassing a safety light curtain raises significant machine-safety and regulatory considerations (e.g., ISO 12100, ISO 13849, EN 201, OSHA requirements). Any such system should be reviewed to ensure that the alternative monitoring means provides an equivalent or higher safety-integrity level and that the bypass is only permitted in appropriately controlled operating modes.

# Position-Monitoring System for Injection-Molding Machine Closing Unit

## Summary

The present invention relates to a position-monitoring system for the closing unit of an injection-molding machine, and more particularly to a system configured to monitor and control the relative positioning of a molding tool during a bumping step of a mold-closing operation. The molding tool comprises cooperating mold halves that, when brought together, define a mold cavity for receiving molten material. In accordance with the invention, a programmable logic controller (PLC) is operatively coupled to a mold-open controller (MOC) to govern the incremental advancement of the molding tool toward a fully closed position. During the bumping step, in which the mold halves are repeatedly and partially advanced to permit venting of trapped gases and controlled degassing from the mold cavity, the system continuously monitors a spacing gap defined between the confronting faces of the mold halves. The PLC, in communication with the MOC, is configured to compare the monitored spacing gap against a predetermined maximum allowable spacing gap, and to selectively interrupt, arrest, or otherwise modify the closing operation in the event that the monitored spacing gap exceeds said maximum allowable spacing gap, thereby preventing improper tool positioning, mitigating the risk of tool damage, and ensuring the integrity of the resulting molded article.

# Technical Description: Injection-Molding Tool Position Monitoring System with Bumping Process Safety Control

## Field of Invention

This invention relates to safety and quality-control systems for injection-molding machines, specifically an apparatus and method for monitoring the relative position of tool halves during the bumping (breathing/degassing) process, wherein the system automatically halts machine operation upon detection of a gap exceeding a predefined maximum threshold.

## Background

During injection molding, the "bumping" process—also known as tool breathing or degassing—involves deliberately opening the mold a small, controlled distance to allow trapped gases to escape, thereby preventing defects such as burn marks, incomplete fills, and dieseling. Precise control of this gap is critical: insufficient opening fails to vent gases, while excessive opening risks material flash, tool damage, or unsafe operating conditions. This invention provides continuous, real-time monitoring to ensure the bumping gap remains within acceptable tolerances.

## System Overview

The monitoring system comprises three principal subsystems integrated through a central control architecture:

1. **Distance measurement subsystem** (distance sensors)
2. **Optical safety barrier** (light curtain)
3. **Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)** as the central processing and control unit

---

## Component Descriptions

### 1. Distance Sensors

The system employs **at least two distance sensors** mounted to measure the relative displacement between the fixed (stationary) mold half and the moving mold half.

**Sensor characteristics:**
- **Type:** Non-contact inductive, laser-triangulation, or eddy-current sensors are preferred for their high resolution and immunity to contamination in the molding environment.
- **Resolution:** Preferably ≤ 5 µm to detect fine variations in the bumping gap.
- **Measurement range:** Typically 0–10 mm, matched to the expected bumping displacement range.
- **Mounting:** Sensors are affixed rigidly to the stationary platen or tool half, with the measurement target being a reference surface on the moving tool half.
- **Redundancy:** Dual sensors positioned at opposing corners or diagonal points enable detection of both parallel gap increase and **tool tilt/skew** (non-parallel opening), which single-point measurement cannot capture.

Each sensor outputs a continuous analog signal (e.g., 4–20 mA or 0–10 V) or a digital signal (e.g., IO-Link) corresponding to the instantaneous gap distance, transmitted to the PLC.

### 2. Light Curtain

A **safety light curtain** is positioned across the mold access area to provide personnel protection and to serve as a secondary interlock during the monitored process.

**Light curtain characteristics:**
- **Configuration:** Transmitter/receiver pair generating an array of parallel infrared beams forming a sensing field across the mold opening zone.
- **Safety rating:** Type 4 per IEC 61496-1/-2, suitable for the highest risk-reduction category.
- **Resolution:** Finger or hand detection resolution (e.g., 14 mm or 30 mm) depending on the required safety distance.
- **Function:** Interruption of any beam generates an Output Signal Switching Device (OSSD) signal to the PLC. During the bumping process, this ensures no personnel intrusion coincides with tool movement, and provides an independent trigger path for machine shutdown.

### 3. Programmable Logic Controller (PLC)

The **PLC** functions as the central processing and control unit, receiving inputs from both the distance sensors and the light curtain, executing the monitoring logic, and issuing control commands to the injection-molding machine.

**PLC characteristics:**
- **Type:** Safety-rated PLC (Safety PLC) compliant with IEC 61508 (SIL 2/3) and ISO 13849 (Performance Level d/e).
- **Inputs:** Analog/digital inputs for the distance sensors; safety-rated OSSD inputs for the light curtain.
- **Outputs:** Safety relay outputs controlling the machine's hydraulic/electric drive enable circuit and the emergency-stop chain.
- **Processing cycle:** Deterministic scan time (e.g., ≤ 10 ms) to ensure rapid response.

---

## Operational Method

The monitoring and shutdown sequence proceeds as follows:

1. **Parameter configuration:** An operator sets a **maximum permissible gap value (G_max)** in the PLC, corresponding to the largest safe/acceptable bumping displacement for the specific tool and material.

2. **Continuous measurement:** During the bumping process, the distance sensors continuously measure the actual gap (G_actual) between the tool halves and transmit these values to the PLC.

3. **Comparison logic:** The PLC compares each sensor's G_actual against G_max in real time. In the dual-sensor configuration, the PLC additionally evaluates the differential between sensors to detect tool tilt exceeding a defined angular tolerance.

4. **Threshold evaluation:**
   - If **G_actual ≤ G_max** at all sensors, the process continues normally.
   - If **G_actual > G_max** at any sensor, or if the differential exceeds the tilt tolerance, the PLC identifies a fault condition.

5. **Shutdown execution:** Upon detecting a fault condition—or upon interruption of the light curtain—the PLC de-energizes the safety output, thereby:
   - Halting the mold movement,
   - Disabling the injection and clamp drives,
   - Triggering a safe stop of the machine (Category 0 or 1 stop per IEC 60204-1).

6. **Fault indication and logging:** The PLC generates a fault signal (visual/audible alarm, HMI message) indicating the cause (gap exceedance, tilt fault, or light-curtain interruption) and logs the event with timestamp and measured values for diagnostic and quality-traceability purposes.

---

## Advantages

- **Process quality assurance:** Ensures the bumping gap remains within tolerance, preventing flash, tool damage, and part defects.
- **Machine and tool protection:** Prevents excessive tool opening that could cause mechanical damage or unsafe conditions.
- **Personnel safety:** The light curtain provides a redundant, safety-rated interlock.
- **Tilt/skew detection:** Multi-point sensing captures non-parallel mold movement undetectable by single-point systems.
- **Traceability:** Event logging supports quality documentation and process optimization.

---

*Note: This description provides a general technical framework. For patent filing, prosecution, or formal disclosure, I recommend consulting a qualified patent attorney to ensure proper claim drafting, prior-art assessment, and compliance with jurisdictional requirements.*

# FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to injection-molding machines, and more particularly to systems and methods for securing and monitoring the closing unit and tool area of such machines. Specifically, the invention pertains to the safeguarding and control of a defined spacing gap between mold parts (mold halves) following the buildup of closing pressure during an injection-molding cycle.

In the field of injection-molding technology, a closing unit is employed to bring together and hold closed the cooperating mold parts of a molding tool under substantial clamping force, thereby resisting the internal pressures generated when molten material is injected into the mold cavity. The tool area, in which these mold parts move relative to one another, represents a region of significant mechanical activity and potential hazard, necessitating reliable safety and monitoring arrangements to protect operating personnel and to ensure proper functioning of the machine.

More particularly, the invention concerns the maintenance and precise control of a spacing gap that is established between the mold parts after the closing pressure has been built up. In certain molding processes and machine configurations, it is desirable to retain a controlled clearance or gap between the mold parts, or between components of the closing unit, even after clamping pressure has been applied. The present invention addresses the need to monitor such a spacing gap, to detect deviations therein, and to control the associated components of the closing unit so as to maintain the gap within predetermined tolerances, thereby enhancing both the operational safety and the process reliability of the injection-molding machine.
